item.title: An Auditable Multi-Agent Forum for Scientific Workflows with a Computational MOF Case Study
item.description: Scientific research increasingly combines large language models, computational tools and automated laboratories, creating a need to link hypotheses, assumptions, artifacts and revisions. We present Core-Forum, a persistent multi-agent forum architecture designed to organize these records in a common research thread. item.title: When, Where, and How Experience Becomes Structure: Mechanisms for Recursive Self-Improvement in LLM Agents
item.description: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) studies how AI systems modify themselves and carry those changes into the generation of subsequent improvements. LLM agents can pursue this process by using interaction experience to revise Prompt, Memory, Skill, and Harness in some cases while keeping the task-execution model’s weights fixed. item.title: Self-directed coaching: repositioning the client as the internalizing agent of developmental self-regulation a conceptual framework and research agenda for coaching theory and practice
item.description: Coaching has become one of the most widely deployed developmental interventions in organizational, educational, and health-professions settings, and the literature offers substantial evidence for its short-term benefits. Evidence on whether those benefits persist after formal coaching support is withdrawn is thinner and less systematic, and the question points to an unresolved tension at the field’s core. item.title: Post-Training on the Clock: Specializing a Small Language Model on a Consumer GPU
item.description: Abstract How should a language model be specialized for a target task when training is limited to one consumer GPU and a few hours? We study the allocation of a nominal three-hour training budget, with up to 0.3 additional hours, between supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). item.title: KAIROS: Stateful, Context-Aware Power-Efficient Agentic Inference Serving
item.description: Power has become a central bottleneck for AI inference. This problem is becoming more urgent as agentic AI emerges as a major workload class, yet prior power-management techniques focus almost entirely on single-turn LLM serving. item.description: Abstract The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in higher education has created a significant assessment gap, as students increasingly submit AI-assisted work without demonstrating competencies required to verify facts, authenticate sources, identify hallucinations, assess bias, uphold academic integrity, and critically reflect on AI use. item.description: Recent advances in large language models have enabled a new class of agentic data science systems that allow users to complete complex data science workflows through natural language. item.description: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is a life-limiting autosomal recessive disorder caused by biallelic loss-of-function mutations in the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) gene, most commonly F508del. item.title: Evaluation of state-of-the-art models for improving the diagnosis of mango tree diseases through supervised learning of symptom images in Burkina Faso
item.description: Abstract In Burkina Faso, the mango industry faces numerous phytosanitary constraints. This situation is exacerbated by producers’ lack of knowledge about diseases and their symptoms and the low uptake of control technologies. This study aims to develop a tool using artificial intelligence-based approaches for better integrated management of the main diseases affecting mango trees. item.description: Abstract This narrative literature review examines published peer-reviewed research from 2012 to 2024 on feedback originating from e-assessment and e-tasks in the context of secondary and university mathematics teaching. item.title: Viewpoints on inclusive education at the end of initial teacher preparation: Q methodology research
item.description: Abstract This study used Q methodology to explore the perspectives on inclusive education held by 44 student teachers completing their initial teacher education (ITE) programme at Qatar University. Participants ranked 44 statements along a quasi‐normal distribution; factor analysis yielded four distinct viewpoints. item.description: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. item.description: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. item.title: From Coding to Creativity: Integrating Design Thinking into IT and Technology Education
item.description: This study examines how the integration of Design Thinking into Information Technology (IT) and technology education can bridge technical programming skills and creative, human-centered problem-solving.
